originalTitle: Lohia Corp IPO opens on July 23: Here’s all you need to know
simplifiedContent: Lohia Corp, a company that makes machinery for technical textiles, is going to start selling its shares to the public for the first time through an Initial Public Offering (IPO) on July 23. This means that the company's existing shareholders will be selling some of their shares to new investors. The company has been doing well, with its profit increasing by 64% and revenue going up by 25% in the last financial year. This IPO might be of interest to investors who want to buy shares in a company with a strong recent performance. The IPO will allow investors to buy over 2.59 crore shares from the existing shareholders.

originalTitle: JK Cement Q1 profit drops 15.3% YoY to Rs 274.62 crore
simplifiedContent: JK Cement, a company that makes cement, just reported their profits for the first quarter of the year. Unfortunately, they made 15.3% less profit compared to the same time last year, with a profit of Rs 274.62 crore. However, the company's overall sales, or revenue, actually increased by 20.25% to Rs 4,031.72 crore. The reason their profit went down is that their expenses, or costs, rose by 25.5%, which is more than their sales increase. This means that even though they sold more, their costs went up even more, resulting in lower profit.

originalTitle: RBL Bank Q1 Results: Net profit rises 27% YoY to Rs 254 crore; Emirates NBD ownership boosts growth outlook
simplifiedContent: RBL Bank just released its quarterly results, and its profit increased by 27% compared to the same time last year, reaching Rs 254 crore. This is a significant improvement, and the bank's income from interest on loans also went up by 12%. The bank's ownership by Emirates NBD is expected to help it grow even more, especially in areas like corporate banking and international trade. This is good news for the bank and could be positive for investors. The bank's management is expecting strong growth in the future, which could be beneficial for those who have invested in the bank.

originalTitle: IPO GMP Check: SBI Funds Management IPO vs Alpine Texworld IPO - What grey market signals ahead of listings?
simplifiedContent: Two companies, SBI Funds Management and Alpine Texworld, recently finished their initial public offering (IPO) process, which allows them to raise money from investors. SBI Funds Management had a lot of interest, with 41.66 times more people wanting to buy shares than were available, and its "grey market premium" (a measure of expected price) was ₹91. In contrast, Alpine Texworld had much less interest, with only 1.40 times more people wanting to buy shares than available, and its grey market premium was much lower at ₹1. This suggests that investors are expecting SBI Funds Management to do well when its shares start trading, while Alpine Texworld may not do as well. The grey market premium is an indicator of how the company's shares might perform when they are listed on the stock market.

originalTitle: ICICI Bank Q1 Results 2026: Net profit rises 16% to  ₹14,804.50 crore
simplifiedContent: ICICI Bank just announced its financial results for the first quarter of 2026. The bank made a net profit of ₹14,804.50 crore, which is 16% more than it made in the same period last year. This means the bank's profit increased by ₹2,036.29 crore compared to last year. This increase is a good sign for the bank and its investors, as it shows the bank is performing well. The bank shared this news on July 18, 2026, giving investors an update on its financial health.

originalTitle: Yes Bank Q1 results 2026: Net profit jumps 33.7% YoY, operating profit up 25.5%
simplifiedContent: Yes Bank, a bank in India, just released its financial results for the first quarter of 2026. The bank made a net profit of ₹1,071 crore, which is 33.7% more than what it made during the same time last year. This is a significant increase and a good sign for the bank. The bank's operating profit also went up by 25.5%, which is another positive indicator. This increase in profit is important because it shows that the bank is performing well, which can be good news for people who have invested in the bank's stock.
